title: API incident autopsy and mitigation notes (timeouts / 429s / degraded streaming / surge errors)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, writable autopsy + mitigation notes doc for on-call SREs to capture quick findings and suggested runbook steps for common API degradations: client-side timeouts, 429s (rate-limited traffic), degraded streaming (stalls / partial responses), and elevated 5xx/4xx error rates. Use during or immediately after incident triage and keep terse – this is intentionally more pragmatic than the formal postmortem template.

Quick index (jump to):
- Incident triage checklist (what to check first)
- Short mitigation recipes by symptom (timeouts, 429s, streaming stalls, error spikes)
- Root-cause hypothesis matrix (what typically causes each symptom)
- Helpful dashboard / log queries and thresholds to eyeball
- Escalation / rollback playbook (who to call, what to change)
- Example incident summary snippets for postmortems
- Action items / unresolved questions (to convert into JIRA)

---
INCIDENT TRIAGE CHECKLIST (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm scope: which endpoints, regions, customers affected (check traffic by route / api_key).
- Check high-level KPIs: 5xx rate, 4xx rate, median latency, p95/p99 latency, streaming stalls count.
- Look for correlated infra signals: GPU host CPU/memory pressure, pod restarts, OOMs, node autoscaler events, AZ/region networking alerts.
- Check quota / config changes: recent deploys, rollout percentages, feature flags, rate limit config changes, infra scaling policy edits.
- If streaming degraded: check chunking throughput and per-connection window sizes, proxy timeouts, and any websocket/frame errors.
- If 429s: verify global vs per-customer rate limiter, token bucket exhaustion, quota DB latency, and any sudden spike in legitimate traffic or retry storms.
- Take initial communication step: open incident Slack channel, post short status (scope, impact, mitigation in progress).

---
MITIGATION RECIPES (quick, low-risk first):
Symptom: Client timeouts / high request latency
- Immediate probes: curl a few affected endpoints from multiple regions; run k6/lightweight synthetic to reproduce.
- Quick mitigations: scale up the backend pool (increase replica count / warm up extra GPU slots), temporarily increase request timeout and client-side retry backoff recommendations, enable fast-fail responses for known expensive routes.
- Longer quick-fix: revert recent model or runtime change if coincident with onset; switch routing policy to lower-cost / cached model variant.
- Avoid: making aggressive global config changes without throttling (can worsen cascading failures).

Symptom: Elevated 429s (rate limit errors)
- Immediate probes: query rate limiter metrics (tokens per second, refill rates), inspect quota DB latency, check for recent token-bucket config changes, and inspect client retry patterns in logs.
- Quick mitigations: temporarily raise per-customer or global rate limits for impacted customers (prefer per-key exceptions), enable burst capacity if configured, add short-lived bypass for internal CI traffic.
- If originating from a bugged client: block or throttled IPs at edge for noisy clients; contact customer via CS if needed.
- If caused by retry storms: add randomized jitter to retry logic and enable early circuit breakers.

Symptom: Degraded streaming (stalling partial responses / premature connection closes)
- Immediate probes: check proxy/nginx/alb timeouts, connection counts, keepalive settings, and server-side generator logs for token emission pauses.
- Quick mitigations: increase proxy read_timeout / keepalive for streaming endpoints, reduce chunk size or switch to chunked encoding with explicit flush, fall back to non-streaming (blocking) variant for critical customers.
- If KV cache or stateful resource is slow: fail open to a cached response or shorter-prefix cache; reduce parallel KV lookups.

Symptom: Elevated 5xx error rate
- Immediate probes: fetch error logs (stack traces), map errors to codepaths (model load failures, OOM, CUDA errors, panics), and correlate with deploys or infra events.
- Quick mitigations: roll back the most recent deploy, mark unhealthy hosts out of load balancer, drain and restart problematic pods, and enable a compatible fallback model.

---
ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS MATRIX (common causes)
- Timeouts: overloaded GPU hosts; model runtime regressions (new kernels); slow external dependencies (KMS, quota DB); degraded autoscaler tuning.
- 429s: misconfigured rate-limits after a rollout; global traffic spike; retry storms from clients following transient errors; shared global quota exhaustion.
- Streaming stalls: proxy timeouts; resource contention on event loop; backpressure mis-negotiation between runtime and transport; kernel-level stalls during long-context generation.
- 5xx spikes: bad model artifact / mismatch with runtime; OOM/driver issues; corrupted weights; sudden disk I/O errors for VM-backed caches.

---
USEFUL DASHBOARD PANELS & LOG QUERIES
- Grafana panels: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-route 4xx/5xx counts, connections by gateway, GPU host load, autoscaler events.
- Example log query (ELK): "status:[500 TO 599] AND route:\"/v1/generate\" | stats count() by error_type, model_version"
- Rate limiter query: "sum(rate(tokens_consumed[1m])) by api_key" and "avg(latency_quota_db_ms) by instance"
- Streaming probe: count of active streams with no output for >5s: "stream_event | where time_since_last_chunk > 5000"

---
ESCALATION & ROLLBACK PLAYBOOK
- Triage owner (SRE on-call) to assign incident severity.
- If impact is P1: page on-call mobile list, call product PM and engineering on-call for model/runtime.
- Quick rollback checklist: identify deploy ID -> verify canary % -> trigger rollback in deploy system -> monitor error-rate drop in 5 minutes.
- If rollback not possible: switch routing to stable model variant and set conservative autoscaling (increase min_replicas).
- Communicate: update incident channel every 15 minutes with scope and mitigation status; post an initial incident summary to the #incidents channel within 60 minutes.

---
EXAMPLE INCIDENT SUMMARY (pasteable into postmortem template)
- Incident title: Elevated 5xx and timeouts for /v1/completions in US-West (2025-05-28 09:12–10:03 UTC)
- Impact: 23% requests returned 5xx during a 51-minute window; multiple customers experienced request timeouts (~p95 latency rose to 12s).
- Root cause (hypothesis): new runtime kernel selection introduced an allocation pattern causing memory pressure on 1 GPU family -> OOMs and retries.
- Mitigation: rolled back runtime commit 0a1b2c -> error rate returned to baseline within 8 minutes.
- Next steps: add canary in multiple regions, add memory-pressure alerting for kernel paths, open JIRA ticket to add regression test.

---
ACTION ITEMS / UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (convert to JIRA)
- Add a synthetic test for streaming chunk cadence to detect stalls (owner: Marco; due: 2025-06-10).
- Audit rate limiter configs across all models and add per-customer exception path (owner: Elena; due: 2025-06-15).
- Investigate whether quota DB peering in us-west requires a read-replica for peak traffic (owner: infra; due: 2025-06-20).
- Add a short runbook snippet to production runbooks for immediate model fallback steps (owner: SRE docs; due: 2025-06-05).

---
NOTES TO SELF / ON-CALL HINTS
- When in doubt, prefer minimal blast radius actions: scale up or add per-key exceptions rather than flipping global flags.
- Keep a copy of the last-known-good model artifact id handy in incident channels.
- Watch for retry loops: sometimes client libraries will retry too aggressively; adding a temporary 429 with Retry-After can calm the storm.
- Use 'kubectl rollout undo' sparingly—verify runtime compatibility first.

If you used this doc during an incident, paste the final timeline snippet into the formal postmortem and link the incident Slack thread and any JIRA tickets.

Unresolved: need to decide canonical alert thresholds for streaming stalls (p95 chunk gap > 3s?) — propose in next SRE sync.

End of doc.
